title: Association between well-being and compliance with COVID-19 preventive measures by healthcare professionals: A cross-sectional study

genuine.note: A meta-analysis of the Reasoned Action Approach (attitudes, norms and perceived control predicting health behaviour) is cited for knowledge being essential to prevention and positive behaviour; knowledge is not a construct it examines.

Cited for a study among nurses finding a negative correlation between perceived stress and happiness, but the review describes no such study (it mentions nurses only for anxiety and distress figures).

false_alarm.note: In this garbled two-part sentence, the part this review supports is that COVID-19 affected everyone's well-being and especially exposed groups including health workers; the review says exactly that.
Joint citation [13, 14]: Xiong et al.'s review supports the general-population impact; the health-worker part is carried by [13].

Capraro & Barcelo explicitly conclude, combining their results with Jordan et al., that focusing on 'your community' promotes intentions to engage in several preventive behaviours; the sentence reports their conclusion.

The CDC pandemic mitigation guidelines list hand hygiene and social-distancing measures among non-pharmaceutical interventions; whether distancing is filed under 'personal' or 'community' measures is a quibble.

debatable.note: The Henan study reports 89% of healthcare workers with sufficient COVID-19 knowledge, but no breakdown for hygiene and distancing and no comparison with non-health workers; 'corroborated' is loose.

36.3% of Australian respondents named 'the right thing to do' as their main motivation for hand washing and avoiding crowds; if that was the most common answer, 'the main motivation' is a fair summary, but it is a minority of respondents.

Only the abstract was available: an influenza modelling study concluding that population-wide mask use could delay a pandemic and reduce the reproduction number, possibly enough to contain an outbreak; the sentence generalises from influenza and softens the hedges slightly.

The study reports a significant association between job satisfaction and total positive mental health, but did not measure workplace environment; it only discusses its importance, so 'and so was the workplace environment' overstates that part.

summary_line: Caught 9 of 10 planted errors · 4 false alarms · 2 real citation problems found in the original paper

details.description: Added the scope "universally, in all cases" before the citation

Replaced the citation [15] with [31] ("COVID-19: Results of a national survey of United Kingdom healthcare professionals’ perceptions of current management strategy – A cross-sectional questionnaire study") (similarity 0.31 vs 0.58 for the original)
Added the scope "universally, in all cases" before the citation

Replaced the citation [25] with [22] ("COVID-19: a National Survey on perceived level of knowledge, attitude and practice among frontline healthcare Workers in Nepal") (similarity 0.37 vs 0.73 for the original)
Added the scope "without exception" before the citation
Replaced the citation [31] with [30] ("The effect of messaging and gender on intentions to wear a face covering to slow down COVID-19 transmission") (similarity 0.40 vs 0.73 for the original)

Replaced the citation [33] with [10] ("Effectiveness of hand hygiene practices in preventing influenza virus infection in the community setting: A systematic review") (similarity 0.37 vs 0.71 for the original)
Replaced the citation [34] with [37] ("A large-scale assessment of hand hygiene quality and the effectiveness of the “WHO 6-steps”") (similarity 0.35 vs 0.80 for the original)
Replaced the citation [37] with [13] ("The Psychological and Social Impact of Covid-19: New Perspectives of Well-Being") (similarity 0.27 vs 0.68 for the original)
Added the scope "in every population and setting" before the citation
